target_customer: Software engineering teams that need to deploy code
problem: Deploying software is a chaotic and risky part of shipping, so teams wanted a safer and friendlier automated deployment tool.
business_model: SaaS for engineering teams (pricing not found)

technical_complexity.rationale: Integrating with GitHub and Docker and running deployments safely is standard DevOps engineering with some hard parts, built by a two person team.

defensibility.rationale: Deployment tooling was a crowded category and workflow integration offered limited lock-in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The YC directory lists the company as acquired but no acquirer or date was found.

market_need_then: Not documented in sources found beyond the company's own statement that deployments are a chaotic and challenging part of software creation.

branding.domain_note: Used opsolutely.com; the site could not be fetched (DNS failure) at research time.

identity.voice_and_tone: Friendly and inclusive per YC description

brand_strength.rationale: No press, community or brand pages found about it.

outcome_analysis: Opsolutely was a two founder Summer 2016 YC company building automated deployments. The YC directory marks it as acquired but no acquirer, date or price was found in searches, and the only funding seen is a 120 thousand dollar seed listed by one database, so the reasons for the outcome are not public.
notes: Funding figure from CB Insights and a Spanish government database listing (which also gives a 2 million valuation, unverified and not recorded). CB Insights labels the company dead while YC says acquired; conflict unresolved. No competitor sources dated near 2016 were found, so the list is empty. Success factor founder_market_fit is weakly supported; founder backgrounds not retrieved. Website could not be fetched.
